title: Coffee and cardamom cake
subtitle: Turkish-spiced coffee loaf with cardamom frosting
excerpt: Coffee and cardamom are a pairing from the Turkish and Middle Eastern café tradition, where cardamom pods are ground into the coffee itself. This loaf cake builds on that combination, strong coffee in the sponge, cardamom in both the batter and the frosting. The result is a cake that smells intensely aromatic when it comes out of the oven and tastes more complex than a standard coffee cake.
sourceNotes: The flavour pairing of coffee and cardamom is rooted in the Middle Eastern and North African tradition of qahwa, in which cardamom pods are simmered with coffee as part of the brewing process. This practice spread westward through the Ottoman Empire and appears in Turkish coffee culture as well. The application of this pairing to a baked loaf cake is a contemporary British home baking adaptation, following the broader trend of Middle Eastern flavours entering mainstream baking from the 2010s onward. The frosting here uses cardamom cream cheese rather than plain buttercream, a version that became popular through food blog recipes from about 2015.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the unfrosted cake, well wrapped, for up to 2 months.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bake the day before and store in an airtight tin. Frost on the day of serving.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: conventional 170°C or fan 150°C; a skewer in the centre should come out clean

content.text: Coffee and cardamom cake smells remarkable before it even reaches the oven, the cardamom and espresso together have an intensity that a plain coffee cake doesn't. Use strong espresso or very strongly brewed filter coffee, not instant. The cardamom cream cheese frosting is optional but recommended; it adds another layer of the spice and softens the cake's edge.

items.prepNote: cooled strong espresso or very strong filter coffee

content.text: For the cardamom cream cheese frosting

Preheat the oven to 170°C conventional (150°C fan). Grease and line a 900 g loaf tin. Cream the butter and brown sugar together until pale and fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time. Stir in the cooled espresso. Fold in the flour, baking powder, and cardamom until just combined, don't overmix. Spoon into the tin and bake for 50 to 55 minutes until risen and a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean. Cool in the tin for 15 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack.

Beat the cream cheese until smooth. Add the sifted icing sugar and the cardamom, then beat until combined and creamy. Spread thickly over the top of the cooled cake, letting it drift slightly down the sides. Dust with a little extra ground cardamom to finish.
